      "arc_panel_motif_component_matching_heuristic": {
        "id": "arc_panel_motif_component_matching_heuristic",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC panel-and-motif composition: try 4-connected component matching",
        "content": "For ARC tasks with large solid-color panels containing scattered background-color cells and smaller motifs on that same background, consider matching panels to motifs by the number of 4-connected components formed by the anomalous/background cells—not just by hole count or mask overlap. If supported by the examples, preserve the panel layout, place each motif inside a one-cell border of the panel color, and recolor motif-background cells to that panel color. This is a task-family heuristic, not a universal ARC rule; verify it against demonstrations before applying. Evidence: task-9a25a41d’s component-count matching produced the correct composition after several overlap- and count-based assignments failed.",

      "arc_marker_selected_boundary_contour_heuristic": {
        "id": "arc_marker_selected_boundary_contour_heuristic",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC marker-selected boundary contour recoloring",
        "content": "For ARC puzzles matching the demonstrated pattern, where 8 is background, 1 is an obstacle, 6 is a marker, and 7 is the contour color: find the 4-connected component of 8/background containing 6. Preserve all 1s and the 6. Recolor to 7 the cells in that selected component that lie on the grid edge or are 8-neighbor adjacent to a 1-cell in a 4-connected component of 1s that touches the grid boundary. Leave other cells unchanged. This rule matched the three demonstrations and produced the correctly submitted test output for task-5b079f52. Keep this heuristic separate from panel-and-motif component matching; verify the topology and color roles against examples before applying it.",

      "arc_quadrant_pattern_tile_transform": {
        "id": "arc_quadrant_pattern_tile_transform",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC quadrant-pattern tile transform",
        "content": "For ARC puzzles with four 4x4 panels, test this rule against demonstrations: the counts of non-background cells in the top-left and top-right panels may specify output height and width, respectively. Construct the output by repeating the bottom-right 4x4 panel with row/column indices modulo 4. Preserve its non-background cells; at background cells, use the corresponding bottom-left panel cell with the same modulo-4 coordinates. Verify the background color, panel roles, dimension counts, and output rule on examples before applying; empty top panels may follow special behavior.",

      "arc_framed_panel_rowwise_outlier_extraction": {
        "id": "arc_framed_panel_rowwise_outlier_extraction",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC framed-panel row-wise outlier extraction",
        "content": "For ARC puzzles with grids tiled into framed panels, test whether demonstrations show one panel per panel row being selected because its object-cell pattern differs from the others in that row. Compare panel interiors by exact cell pattern, extract the demonstrated unique outlier from each row, and preserve its framing/background when stacking the selected panels vertically. Validate panel dimensions, output boundaries, and that each selected panel is the row-wise outlier before applying the rule to the test grid.",

      "arc_marker_guided_bar_serpentine_contour": {
        "id": "arc_marker_guided_bar_serpentine_contour",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC marker-guided serpentine contour around 1/2 bars",
        "content": "For ARC puzzles with background 8, a single 3 marker, and straight bars made of 1s and 2s, test this rule against the demonstrations: recolor all 1 cells to 2, then draw a 3-colored serpentine contour on the marker-facing side of the bars. For each bar, let k be its count of 1 cells; the contour rail is offset by k+1 from the relevant bar boundary, extends along the bar axis by the corresponding offset, and connects around successive bars. Derive the correct boundary, endpoint, and turn direction from the marker’s position and the demonstrations rather than assuming a midpoint. In the validated instance, the left contour boundary was the upper bar’s start minus (k+1), not a midpoint inferred from the lower bar. Preserve existing 2s and the marker; verify the complete path on all examples before applying it.",

      "arc_divided_panels_corner_marker_nested_patterns": {
        "id": "arc_divided_panels_corner_marker_nested_patterns",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC divided panels with corner-marker patterns",
        "content": "For ARC grids partitioned by straight divider lines, test whether individual panels are filled with nested rectangular bands or other patterns determined by colored cells placed diagonally from a panel corner. Use demonstrations to infer panel bounds, corner orientation, and the marker-to-band color sequence; preserve divider lines. Do not assume one marker produces alternating bands: in the demonstrated task, a panel with a single marker was filled uniformly with that marker's color. Leave unmarked panels unchanged as the background only if examples support that behavior. Validate the complete proposed transformation against all examples before submission.",

      "arc_hollow_frame_solid_block_pairing": {
        "id": "arc_hollow_frame_solid_block_pairing",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC hollow-frame and solid-block pairing",
        "content": "For ARC puzzles containing equal-size hollow square frames and solid square blocks, test whether the output arranges the two categories in adjacent columns, one object per horizontal band. Classify hollow frames by their empty interiors and solid blocks by their filled interiors; do not mistake frames for solid blocks. Order each category independently by reading order (top-to-bottom, then left-to-right). Each band places the next frame on the left and the next solid block on the right. If the categories have different counts, pad the shorter column with background; the number of bands is the larger category count. In the demonstrated task, frames 9, 7, 8 paired in order with solid blocks 6, 1, 2, 4, leaving the final left slot as background. On the test, frames 1, 9, 4 paired with blocks 7, 8, leaving the final right slot as background. Verify object dimensions, ordering, padding, and output dimensions against all demonstrations before applying.",

      "arc_parallel_diagonal_marker_pairwise_span_fill": {
        "id": "arc_parallel_diagonal_marker_pairwise_span_fill",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC fill between parallel diagonal marker lines using all pairs",
        "content": "For ARC puzzles matching the demonstrated pattern—background 8, parallel down-right diagonal marker lines of one color (such as 9), and fill color 2—test this rule against the demonstrations. Represent each marker line by its offset d=c-r and the interval of s=r+c values at its endpoints. For every pair of marker lines, including non-adjacent pairs, fill background cells with 2 when their d lies strictly between the two offsets and their s lies in the intersection of the two lines’ endpoint intervals. Preserve all marker cells and other non-background cells. Testing only adjacent pairs can miss fill regions; validate the all-pairs rule on every demonstration before applying it.",

      "arc_color_matched_motif_panel_carving": {
        "id": "arc_color_matched_motif_panel_carving",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC color-matched motif carving in solid panels",
        "content": "For ARC puzzles with small 3×3 colored motifs and larger solid square panels in matching colors, test whether each panel is transformed using the same-color motif as a mask: change panel cells at occupied motif positions to the background, leaving cells at blank motif positions in the panel color. Validate the polarity against every demonstration; filled-versus-hole polarity is easy to reverse. Preserve the panels’ relative arrangement and intervening background gaps, and crop the output to the panels with a one-cell background margin when the examples support that layout.",
